clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man presented with one month of hypogastric region discomfort, right lower quadrant colicky pain, pain radiating to the back, 2-3 kg weight loss, and anorexia. An abdominal CT scan revealed a well-demarcated, homogenous solitary mass in the cecum with thickened ileum wall. Biopsy of the mass showed lamina propria infiltrated by PMNCs and eosinophils, with immunohistochemistry positive for vimentin and CD68, negative for C-Kit (CD117), and focally positive for CD34, smooth muscle actin (SMA), and ALK. Following pathological confirmation of Inflammatory Myofibroblastic Tumor (IMT), the patient underwent right hemicolectomy for the cecal mass, which was found to be associated with ileocolic intussusception during surgery.
